title: Capture Free Pieces
subtitle: Spot undefended pieces and take them for free.
goals: Choose the most valuable free piece

steps.say: Most games below master level are decided by one thing: free pieces. A piece with no defender is called 'hanging' — and your job every single move is to scan the board for them. Let's train that eye.

steps.prompt: Black left a piece completely undefended. Find it and take it!
hints: Scan each black piece and ask: who protects it?
The knight on a5 is all alone — and your rook sees the a-file.

line.say: Free knight! Nothing could recapture — three points, zero cost.

steps.wrongSay: There's a whole knight available for free. Scan the black pieces one by one.
steps.successSay: That scan — 'what's undefended?' — should run in your head every move of every game.

steps.prompt: One black piece is hanging. Capture it!
hints: Check each piece's defenders: the c6 knight is guarded by the c8 rook. What about the bishop?
The b5 bishop has no defender — and your queen sees it along the diagonal.

line.say: Exactly! The rook guarded the knight, but nobody guarded the bishop. Free piece.

rejections.say: Nxe5! You placed your knight on a square the c6 knight defends — and missed a free bishop. Scan before you jump.

steps.wrongSay: One black piece has zero defenders. Compare the knight and the bishop carefully.
steps.successSay: Defended vs. undefended — that one distinction wins more games than any opening.

steps.prompt: Two black pieces look loose — but only one is truly free. Grab the bigger prize!
hints: The e6 knight looks tasty for your d4 knight... but check its bodyguards. Pawns count!
The f7 pawn defends e6. Meanwhile your g2 bishop stares down the LONG diagonal — all the way to a8.

line.say: A whole rook! The knight was protected by the f7 pawn, but the rook in the corner had nobody. Five points beats three anyway.

rejections.say: fxe6! The f7 pawn was on guard duty. And even if the knight HAD been free — the undefended rook was worth more. Always take the biggest free piece.

steps.wrongSay: Check defenders on both loose pieces — then take the one that's really free.
steps.successSay: Value check: pawn 1, knight/bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. Always grab the biggest freebie.

steps.prompt: The e5 pawn is attacked twice and defended once. Win it — the full sequence!
hints: Count: your knight and bishop both hit e5; only the d6 pawn defends it. Two attackers vs. one defender — the capture works.
Take with either piece; when Black recaptures, take again. You come out a pawn ahead.

line.say: ...and you take again. Piece for piece, but you pocketed a pawn — because you had MORE attackers than they had defenders.
...and the knight finishes the job. Two attackers beat one defender — you win exactly one pawn.

steps.wrongSay: Count attackers and defenders on e5: 2 vs 1 means the capture succeeds. Start taking!
steps.successSay: Attackers minus defenders — that little bit of arithmetic is the engine behind every safe capture.
